paragraphs: Friend, this one is heavy, so let's sit with it a second. Saul's story ends on Mount Gilboa: his army flees, his sons die, and he dies by his own sword (1 Samuel 31:1-6). I think the quiet lesson is that a life can start with a crown and still end in a hard place. Being chosen is a gift, but it's the walk afterward that matters.

Now look at the people of Jabesh-gilead. The Philistines hang Saul's body on the wall of Beth-shan (1 Samuel 31:10), and the men of valor of Jabesh-gilead journey all night to bring the bodies home (1 Samuel 31:12). Saul had once rescued their town from the Ammonites (1 Samuel 11:1-11). I think they remembered, and they showed up for him when nobody else did. They buried the bones under the tamarisk tree and fasted seven days (1 Samuel 31:13). Kindness you give out can come back around, friend.

And hear me, because the story isn't over. David is down in Ziklag, and he has no idea what happened on that mountain yet. This passage ends the David and Saul story, but it doesn't end the Bible's story of the king God has for His people. So here's what to carry out of my bakery today: be faithful while the oven's still warm, and be loyal to people when it costs you something. I messed up plenty in my days, but I learned that part from watching Jabesh do it.
